scope: One full authorized W4B guide plus one Original C transfer; no segmentation, processing, retry or canonical edit
text:
So my son is obsessed with motorcycles. He calls them motos. That's just what they're called in our house now.

So I wrote him a book about one. There's a moto named Mikey who has decided he'd rather be a car — cars have roofs, cars have four wheels, cars get to go out in the rain. And then an actual car turns up, and she tells him she's spent her whole life wanting to be a moto. They both want to be the thing the other one already is.

And that's the part I care about, because it isn't his name dropped into somebody else's story. Most personalized books are one adventure with a name slot in it. There's no name slot for the thing your kid is actually working through.

So I make them for other people's kids now. You tell me what's going on for them right now, and who's actually in their life. Who does bedtime. Who coaches. And what you want it to look like. And I write the story around that. Then it gets printed once, for one child, and never printed again.
